subject: Global commit split & per-token discount structure for SkylarkAI
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Kai Nakamura <kai@skylarkai.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Global commit split & per-token discount structure for SkylarkAI

Hi Kai,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great to see SkylarkAI's multi-region inference patterns. Per our conversation, I'm sending a compact proposal for how we can structure a hosted API commit that accounts for your US/EU/APAC split and gets you a meaningful per-token discount. Attached are two files: a reference pricing sheet and the MAU/traffic estimates you shared.

High level proposal (fast read):
- Annual committed spend: $360k (committed capacity for hosted API usage)
- Effective per-token tiers: 0-1B tokens = $0.0006/token, 1B-5B = $0.00045/token, 5B+ = $0.00033/token
- Cross-region routing: billing will apply at request time by the region of the serving endpoint. We can set a default routing policy (US primary, EU failover, APAC local) to minimize egress and latency risks.
- Commit split suggestion: 55% US / 30% EU / 15% APAC (based on your estimates). We can make the split a rolling allocation (quarterly adjustment) rather than a hard bucket.

Before I prep formal paperwork: two quick asks from your side —
1) Can you confirm whether the 15% APAC estimate is strictly Japan + APAC pilot, or if you expect growth into Australia/SEA in year 1?
2) Do you need a single global discount applied to invoices, or separate regional credits (some customers prefer separate EMEA/ANZ POs)?

If that looks directionally right, I'll loop Laura for approval on a one-time onboarding credit and Priyom to confirm the routing/billing behavior.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(d) 415-555-0192 | dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-pricing-2026-q4.pdf (pricing matrix)
Attachment: skylark-mau-estimates.xlsx (customer-provided MAU + regional split)
From: Kai Nakamura <kai@skylarkai.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:02:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Global commit split & per-token discount structure for SkylarkAI

Thanks Dylan — appreciated. Quick answers:
- APAC: initially Japan + small pilot in Singapore; we expect to add AU in Q2 2027 if latency tests go well. Can treat APAC as growth-heavy.
- Billing: Procurement prefers a single global PO if possible, but our legal team may require separate invoicing for EU due to VAT/regulations.

Some clarifying questions from our end:
1) If we route a request from a EU user to the US model instance (for capacity reasons), will that be billed at the EU or US per-token rate?
2) Any difference in per-token accounting for streaming vs non-streaming? We typically stream chat results in our product.
3) If we exceed the committed tier in a month, what is the overage rate and how is it settled?

I'll loop procurement once we have the answers.

— Kai
Kai Nakamura
Head of Platform, SkylarkAI
kai@skylarkai.com
procurement@skylarkai.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Kai Nakamura <kai@skylarkai.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Global commit split & per-token discount structure for SkylarkAI

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 11:02 +0900, Kai wrote:
> If we route a request from a EU user to the US model instance (for capacity reasons), will that be billed at the EU or US per-token rate?

Short answer: billed at the region of the serving endpoint (where the inference runs). If EU traffic is routed to a US instance, it will be billed at the US regional rate.

Details / notes:
- We support request-time routing policies: region_preference (route to local if capacity available), latency_priority (prefers lowest latency), and cost_priority (prefers cheaper region). Billing follows where the request executed.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: token accounting is identical (tokens in + tokens out), streaming doesn't change per-token rates; only the billing unit is the same. There is no separate streaming surcharge.
- Overages: 1) We allow up to 10% monthly buffer over commit at the committed per-token price, 2) beyond that, on-demand overage rate = 1.3x the committed top-tier per-token price for that region, billed monthly. We can write a cap/true-up term into the SOW if you want a firm monthly overage cap.

Happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk these parts.

— Priyom
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Thanks Priyom — that's helpful and matches how I briefed them.

Kai — based on that, here's a slightly updated commitment structure we can present to procurement: 
- Annual commit: $360k, quarterly invoiced (Q1 credit applied at signup)
- Flexible split with quarterly reallocation (start 55/30/15 US/EU/APAC)
- Billing: region-execution pricing (requests executed in EU billed as EU tokens)
- Overage: 10% buffer at committed price, then 1.3x top-tier per-token regional rate
- One-time onboarding credit: $5k (applied to first invoice) — pending Laura's approval

If you confirm the APAC growth plan, I'll prepare an SOW and send a DocuSign link.

Best,
Dylan
